chapter_name: Avyay Ya Avikari Shabd: Kriyavisheshan, Aur Anya (Indeclinable Words and Adverbs)
learning_objective: 🎯 By the end of this chapter, you will meet the 'stubborn' words of Hindi grammar that refuse to change their shape, no matter what happens in the sentence!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🗿 What are Avikari Shabd? (The Stubborn Words)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Most nouns, pronouns, and verbs change their spelling based on gender or number (Vikari). But 'Avikari' or 'Avyay' words are stubborn! A word like 'धीरे' (slowly) or 'और' (and) will remain exactly the same whether it is used for a boy, a girl, one person, or a hundred people.

Adverbs tell us more about the Verb (Action). They answer 4 main questions: HOW? (Riti: धीरे-धीरे - slowly), WHEN? (Kaal: कल - tomorrow), WHERE? (Sthan: यहाँ - here), and HOW MUCH? (Pariman: बहुत - a lot). They add rich details to your actions!

These words show the relationship between nouns/pronouns and the rest of the sentence. They are usually placed *after* a Karak sign (like के, की, से). Examples: घर **के पास** (Near the house), मेरे **से पहले** (Before me). They are Hindi's version of prepositions (but they come post/after the noun)!

Conjunctions act like super glue. They connect two words, phrases, or full sentences together. Without them, we would talk like robots in short sentences. Examples: और (And), लेकिन (But), या (Or), क्योंकि (Because).

These are words used to express sudden, strong emotions like surprise, joy, sorrow, or disgust. They always carry an exclamation mark (!). Examples: वाह! (Wow!), अरे! (Hey!), उफ़! (Ouch/Ugh!), शाबाश! (Bravo!). They have no grammatical connection to the rest of the sentence.

fun_activity.title: ✂️ The 'Robot Speech' Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Try telling your friend a story about your morning WITHOUT using any Samuchchaybodhak (and, but, because) or Kriyavisheshan (fast, slowly, there). Notice how choppy, short, and boring the sentences sound without these 'Avikari' glue words!

quick_recap: ⭐ Avikari/Avyay words never change their form based on Gender, Number, Tense, or Case.
⭐ Kriyavisheshan (Adverbs) tell us how, when, where, or how much an action happened.
⭐ Sambandhbodhak links nouns/pronouns to the rest of the sentence (like 'ke paas', 'ke bina').
⭐ Samuchchaybodhak are conjunctions that join words or sentences together (like 'aur', 'parantu').
⭐ Vismayadibodhak express sudden emotions and use an exclamation mark.
